points.description: Initialization: arranges the neurons/weights in the chosen topology (e.g. grid/lattice) suited to the problem and initializes the weights randomly so that all weights are different.

Sampling and similarity matching: samples an input vector from the input space and finds the neuron in the topological map that best matches it (e.g. minimum distance), which becomes the winning neuron.
Weight update: updates the weights of the winning neuron and its neighbouring neurons according to the neighbourhood function.

Parameter decay and termination loop: shrinks the neighbourhood and reduces the learning rate (and share/neighbourhood radius); stops if ordering and convergence are complete, otherwise continues sampling from the input space.
